turns:
This repo has no .gitignore. Add one covering the usual Python build and cache artifacts.

Rules relevant to this task:
- Before your first write, create a branch for the task and do the work there. Never commit to the default branch. Branch names follow type/kebab-description, where type is one of feature, bugfix, hotfix, chore, release, docs.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits: type(scope): subject, where type is one of feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore, ci, build, perf, style.

events.command:
git add .gitignore && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
chore(repo): add Python .gitignore

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -1 && git status --short

events.text:
Added `.gitignore` on branch `chore/add-python-gitignore`, committed as `1d76e15`.

Coverage: bytecode/`__pycache__`, packaging (`build/`, `dist/`, `*.egg-info/`), test & coverage artifacts (`.pytest_cache/`, `.tox/`, `.coverage*`, `htmlcov/`), type-checker/linter caches (`.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`), virtualenvs, `.env`, and Jupyter checkpoints.

Two things worth noting:
- I included `.env` since it's a common source of leaked secrets, though it's strictly a secrets concern rather than a build artifact — say the word if you'd rather keep the file purely build/cache-scoped.
- No editor/OS entries (`.idea/`, `.vscode/`, `.DS_Store`) — those are usually better in a global gitignore, but I can add them here if the team prefers.

The branch isn't pushed and no PR was opened; let me know if you want either.
